2026-11-07 / Project Confluence / Development note

Project Confluence — Configurable Facades and Building Assembly

Extending the facade Blueprint with per-cell module selection and using reusable facade actors to assemble an adjustable building corner in Unreal Engine 5.

Compose a facade from different modules

The previous facade prototype repeated a single wall, frame, and glass set across an adjustable grid. To make that grid useful for a building elevation, I added a module choice for each cell. The facade can now combine a standard window, a full-height opening, and a solid wall within the same arrangement. This allows the position and type of each opening to vary within a consistent wall grid.

An integer array stores the module choices. Before generating the facade, the Blueprint checks that the array length matches the number of cells defined by the floor and column counts. I also moved window placement into a reusable function so both opening variants can share the same assembly steps.

Make each facade rebuildable

Once the facade could contain different modules, I moved its generation logic into a callable function, RebuildFacade. It clears the existing Instanced Static Mesh instances before generating the new arrangement. The building Blueprint can use this function to update a child facade’s parameters and rebuild it with the same logic the facade uses on its own.

Assemble a building corner

I used two facade actors to prototype a building corner in BP_ModularBuilding. The Blueprint uses module dimensions to calculate where the second facade sits relative to the first. In the editor test, I changed Building Module Width from 200 to 240 while keeping Width Modules at three. The wider setting increased the spacing between modules and moved the second facade, making the relationship between grid spacing and corner placement visible.

The next step is to test a change in the number of modules across the building (WidthModules). After that change, the facade’s column count, the length of its ModuleTypes array, and the corner position all need to agree. Once that behavior is verified, I can test the prototype against a more representative building layout in Confluence.
